changes: Removed role 'commissioner' from p1: the colophon only says the book is his (पुस्तको ऽयं) and that it was written (लिखितम्), with no causative likhāpitam; role is owner only
Lowered confidence for p1 to low because the name's form and division are uncertain (Bendall prints 'चिन्मिश्र पाकस्य' with a space)
Shortened the evidence and expanded the notes

notes: This is one item of Bendall's composite number Add. 1680 (XXIV): a Bhadracarīpraṇidhānarāja on 6 palm leaves. Bendall reads the date as N.S. 188 = A.D. 1068, which agrees with NS+880. The colophon does not name a scribe. The owner's name is uncertain. Bendall prints 'चिन्मिश्र पाकस्य' with a space, so it may be one compound name, Cinmiśrapāka, or 'Cinmiśra' followed by some other element. It could also be a garbled form of a Newar name. Because he is called upāsaka, '-miśra' here is probably not the brahmin suffix. He is listed only as owner: the text says the book is his ('pustako 'yaṃ') and that it was written ('likhitam'), but nothing shows he commissioned it.
